blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses keep track of every naira spent or earned? The double-entry principle is the key!

blocks.markdown: The double-entry principle is a fundamental concept in accounting that ensures every transaction affects at least two accounts. This principle helps maintain the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

blocks.title: Double-Entry Rule
blocks.text: For every transaction, debit the account receiving value and credit the account giving value.

blocks.markdown: In double-entry accounting, each transaction is recorded in two accounts: one account is debited, and another is credited. This method helps businesses track where money is coming from and where it is going.

blocks.title: Recording a Simple Transaction
blocks.prompt: Record the transaction: Ibrahim buys office supplies worth ₦5,000 on credit.

steps.text: Identify the accounts affected: 'Office Supplies' and 'Accounts Payable'.
Office Supplies account receives value, so it is debited: ₦5,000.
Accounts Payable account gives value, so it is credited: ₦5,000.

blocks.answer: Debit Office Supplies ₦5,000; Credit Accounts Payable ₦5,000.

blocks.markdown: The double-entry system ensures that the accounting equation remains balanced. Every debit entry has a corresponding credit entry, which helps in preparing accurate financial statements.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always ensure that the total debits equal the total credits in your ledger to maintain a balanced trial balance.

points: The double-entry principle requires every transaction to have a debit and a credit entry.
This principle helps maintain the balance of the accounting equation.
